transcript:
Header: 2026-10-12 10:00 UTC | Duration: 60 mins | Attendees: Sam Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Alex Martin (NexaHealth CTO), Jill Park (NexaHealth SRE), Roberto Diaz (NexaHealth ML Eng), Maya Chen (Nexa PM)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect): weekly POC check-in, onboarding still waiting on VPC access, initial hosted benchmarks run, discussed dedicated sizing and KMS questions, agreed on next steps.

00:00:05 - Sam Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I know we're on a tight schedule so we'll try to keep this to the hour. Quick roll call?
00:00:12 - Alex Martin: Alex here, Jill, Roberto, Maya are on my side.
00:00:15 - Jill Park: hi, morning.
00:00:20 - Priya Rao: Priya here from Redwood, I'll cover the benchmark details today.
00:00:25 - Sam Nguyen: Great. Quick agenda: onboarding status, review the initial latency/cost numbers, discuss dedicated vs hosted for the pilot, surface any security blockers, and assign next steps. Sound good?
00:00:35 - Alex Martin: Yep.

00:01:10 - Priya Rao: Alright, first thing onboarding. We still don't have the VPC peering or the service account creds for the private pilot, correct? Jill?
00:01:18 - Jill Park: yeah, sorry. We had the tickets in our infra queue, but they need approval from network ops. I'm pushing it today. I can share the peering IPs by Wednesday, that's 10-14.
00:01:30 - Sam Nguyen: Perfect, that's the gating item for Dedicated or Private. For hosted tests we can continue since those were already run against the Redwood hosted endpoints.

00:02:05 - Roberto Diaz: Quick question on those hosted runs — what config did you use for the model and batch sizes? Our dev tests used a smaller batch and we saw some variance.
00:02:12 - Priya Rao: Good question. For the initial set I ran the Llama-3 derived open model we recommended, quantized, with batch size 8 for throughput tests, and single-request for latency SLOs. Context lengths varied — we ran 512 and a few 2k traces.
00:02:28 - Roberto Diaz: The 2k traces were the main concern — tail latency seemed a little higher than we'd expect.
00:02:33 - Priya Rao: Right, tail latency during the hosted run was around 240-280ms 95th for the 2k traces, with median ~90ms. There's some noise because hosted routing may put you on a shared pool; Dedicated tiling will tighten that. Also we saw improvements when enabling prefix KV cache for repeated prompts.
00:02:52 - Alex Martin: When you say prefix KV cache, is that something we enable in config or is it automatic? We worry about statefulness.
00:03:00 - Priya Rao: It's a runtime config, you can opt into prefix caching for certain routes. It's stateless from customer infra perspective — cache lives in the runtime and can be scoped per-tenant, and cleared on rollout. There's also option to cap cache usage.

00:03:30 - Jill Park: Security question — for key management, are you using our KMS or Redwood's? We need to know for compliance.
00:03:36 - Sam Nguyen: For the Private deployment we support customer-managed KMS (HSM/KMS) and we can integrate with AWS KMS or GCP KMS. For Dedicated we can also arrange customer KMS integration; hosted defaults to Redwood-managed keys unless you bring your own. We'll follow up with the security pack.
00:03:58 - Maya Chen: And audit logs — can we get token-level audit logs, request/response hashing, or redaction?
00:04:06 - Priya Rao: Yes, we provide request traces and token-level cost breakdown in the Console. For PII-sensitive fields we can support response redaction or not persisting full payloads; that's configurable. We'll include the docs in the security deep dive.

00:04:35 - Alex Martin: Back to performance — what's the expected delta between Hosted and Dedicated for 95th latency? Ballpark.
00:04:40 - Priya Rao: From our benchmarks, for comparable hardware and model variant Dedicated typically reduces 95th by ~30-50% because of node isolation and pinned capacity. For heavy 8k contexts you'll see bigger differences due to memory/KV cache locality. But end-to-end numbers also depend on network routing.
00:05:02 - Roberto Diaz: That makes sense. Cost-wise, do we have any roughs for Dedicated vs hosted per-token?
00:05:08 - Sam Nguyen: We shared an initial spreadsheet earlier but I'll re-send a breakdown tied to the sizing plan. Hosted is pure usage-based, Dedicated has reserved monthly commit plus lower marginal per-token costs. We'll send two scenarios: modest pilot (1-2 nodes) and larger pilot (4 nodes).

00:05:45 - Priya Rao: I uploaded the first pass of the benchmark CSV to the folder. Highlights: latency medians look good for small contexts, tail spikes on some 2k/4k traces. We suspect batching behavior under the shared pool and some tokenization outliers. Also the quantized variant reduces memory and improves throughput but can slightly affect quality.
00:06:05 - Roberto Diaz: Are you recommending quantization for our production? We need to maintain medical answer fidelity.
00:06:12 - Priya Rao: For medical domain I'd recommend running an eval set: quantized v.s. fp16 and measure any regression on key prompts. Redwood Optimize can propose quantization levels per workload. For the POC, we can run two parallel variants: quantized for throughput tests and fp16 for quality checks.

00:07:00 - Jill Park: If we move to Dedicated, how does autoscaling work? We need very predictable throughput, occasional bursts.
00:07:07 - Sam Nguyen: Dedicated supports explicit reserved pools with burst capacity options. You can set autoscaling policies by queue length or latency SLOs. There's also an option to have fallback to hosted for bursts. We can set up canary rollouts and fallback policies so you don't lose availability.

00:07:45 - Alex Martin: On the networking front, our infra prefers VPC peering over public endpoints for compliance. Jill will push peering details by Wed. Once peered, what's the typical turnaround to get Dedicated nodes in our region?
00:07:59 - Priya Rao: Once peering and service account are set, provisioning in-region Dedicated nodes takes about 2-3 business days for standard sizes. If you need a custom GPU type we'll need a little more lead time.

00:08:20 - Roberto Diaz: We ran an internal test with 8k context and saw OOM on lower-memory instance types. Can you recommend a quant + kernel combo?
00:08:28 - Priya Rao: Yes — for 8k we recommend 48GB+ GPU with quantization 4-bit + tuned kernels we use in the nv-optimized runtime. We'll propose a profile: model variant A (fp16) on 80GB for quality tests, model variant B (4-bit) on 48GB for cost/throughput. We'll include recommended kernel flags in the benchmark notes.

00:09:05 - Maya Chen: Any compliance docs you can drop now? We need SOC2 and data processing addendum stuff for legal.
00:09:12 - Sam Nguyen: I'll send the SOC2 summary and the standard DPA. Also we'll include details about audit logs, SSO/SAML integration options, and KMS patterns. Expect that in an email today.

00:09:40 - Alex Martin: About the bench CSV — can you add a per-route token-cost breakdown per model? Our finance team asks for that to compare with Anthropic quote.
00:09:48 - Priya Rao: Yes, I'll add a per-route token breakdown and separate out prompt vs completion tokens. I'll also include a CSV with cost assumptions.

00:10:10 - Jill Park: One more infra nit: can Redwood accept an IAM role for service account or do you need key files?
00:10:18 - Sam Nguyen: We can support both. For GCP we prefer Workload Identity or IAM role binding; for AWS we can use assumed role. If you share your preferred pattern we'll align.

00:10:40 - Alex Martin: Okay, sounds like main blockers are VPC peering and the security deep dive. Anything else?
00:10:46 - Priya Rao: From the bench side, we want two more latency runs with the 8k context and 4-bit quant to confirm OOM behavior. Roberto, can you run those and drop the logs?
00:10:55 - Roberto Diaz: Yep, I'll run them today and upload.

00:11:20 - Sam Nguyen: Great. Let's talk timeline and next steps. We'll recap at the end but quick note — we propose a short security deep dive with our security eng and your infra/security folks week of 10/19.
00:11:33 - Maya Chen: Week of 10/19 works. Please include KMS and audit log folks.

00:12:00 - Priya Rao: I'll schedule a benchmark deep dive separate from security; we can go over CSV and kernel flags in detail.

00:12:20 - Alex Martin: Anything on the legal/procurement side? We might need a standard MSA for a pilot.
00:12:27 - Sam Nguyen: We can start with a pilot MSA and PO. I'll loop in Sales Ops after this call and send the starter docs.

00:12:45 - Jill Park: Minor transcription glitch in our notes earlier — when you said "kv cache" some people heard "key cache" — but we got it.
00:12:52 - Priya Rao: ha yes, KV cache as in key-value. We'll include a short doc explaining the eviction and scoping behaviour.

00:13:15 - Priya Rao: Any concerns about data residency? You mentioned some EU-only traffic earlier.
00:13:22 - Alex Martin: For now pilot traffic will be US-only but long term we need regionally isolated deployment for EU patients. We want options for Private deployment in EU region.
00:13:33 - Sam Nguyen: We support regional Private deployments and can bring an on-prem option if required; we'll surface costs in the pricing sheet.

00:14:00 - Maya Chen: Quick ask — can Redwood provide an example of an eval run with medical prompts so we can reproduce quality tests?
00:14:08 - Priya Rao: Yes, we'll share an eval harness and a seed set of prompts in the repo. You can run it against both quantized and fp16 variants.

00:14:30 - Alex Martin: Okay let's do a quick recap and owners.
00:14:33 - Sam Nguyen: Recap: 1) Jill to provide VPC peering and service account by 2026-10-14. 2) Sam to send pricing and MSA starter by 2026-10-15. 3) Priya to upload detailed benchmark CSV and per-route token-cost by 2026-10-16. 4) Roberto to run two more 8k context latency runs and upload logs by 2026-10-16. 5) Schedule security deep dive for week of 10/19. Does that capture it?
00:15:00 - Alex Martin: Yes.
00:15:05 - Jill Park: Yep.
00:15:10 - Sam Nguyen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up over email with the artifacts. If anything changes ping me on Slack.
00:15:18 - Maya Chen: Thanks all.
00:15:20 - Priya Rao: thanks.

00:15:40 - [meeting ends, recording stops]
